title: Competitive Deep Dive
summary: Market analysis of AI advisory competitors and positioning.
content:
AI Advisory Competitive Deep Dive

Prepared by: Elon (System/Infrastructure Agent) Date: 2026-03-10 Purpose: Deep market intelligence on who is actually building and selling AI systems for small businesses right now.

1. Who Is Doing This RIGHT NOW

Tier A: Agencies Selling AI Systems to SMBs (Direct Competitors)

LeftClick AI (leftclick.ai) -- Nick Saraev, Canada

  • Founded by Nick Saraev (27 y/o, 220K YouTube subs, 400K Instagram)
  • AI consulting firm that advises and builds automated systems for small-to-midsized B2B companies
  • Uses a proprietary AI-driven consulting stack
  • Scaled to $72K/month as a service business
  • Tech stack: n8n, Make.com, GPT-4, custom builds
  • Nick also runs Maker School (#1 no-code community on Skool) and 1SecondCopy (content marketplace)
  • Why this matters: Nick is the closest model to what AOM could become. Solo operator, content-driven lead gen, building real systems not just chatbots. But he's Canadian, not construction-focused, and his audience is other agency owners, not SMB clients.
  • URL: https://www.leftclick.ai/

Morningside AI (morningsideai.com) -- Liam Ottley

  • Liam coined the term "AI Automation Agency (AAA)" in May 2023
  • 700K+ YouTube subscribers, 280K+ free Skool community
  • Evolved from AAA model to "AI Transformation Partners" -- strategy, implementation, long-term optimization
  • 40+ employees now
  • Targets enterprises more than SMBs now
  • Also sells AAA Accelerator course ($5,000-$7,000+) teaching others to start AI agencies
  • Why this matters: Liam created the category. His content educated thousands of people who are now competing in this space. Morningside itself moved upmarket to enterprise, but his students are flooding the SMB space.
  • URL: https://www.liamottley.com/

HummingAgent (hummingagent.ai) -- Denver, CO

  • AI automation for businesses, claims 66% operational savings
  • Services: AI voice agents, chatbots, private ChatGPT (company knowledge bases), custom AI solutions
  • Pricing: $200-$50,000+/month depending on scope
  • No monthly SaaS fees (one-time builds)
  • Deployment: 2-4 weeks typical, simple chatbots in days
  • SOC 2 ready infrastructure
  • Why this matters: Real agency doing real builds. Denver-based. Closest geographic competitor (western US). No construction focus though.
  • URL: https://hummingagent.ai

MQLFlow (mqlflow.com) -- Pete Hogg, UK

  • AI automation agency for small businesses
  • Starting at GBP 2,900 ($3,700 USD), day rate GBP 800 ($1,020)
  • Claims 1,200% average ROI for customers
  • Focus: professional services, healthcare, tech, recruitment
  • Tech stack: Zapier, custom AI tools
  • Why this matters: Proven SMB model with strong ROI claims. UK-based so not direct competition, but their pricing validates AOM's range.
  • URL: https://mqlflow.com

Authority AI (authorityai.ai) -- Fort Lauderdale, FL

  • AI bots, AI-powered CRM, custom AI estimators, document generators, internal knowledge bots
  • Targets: law firms, insurance agencies, trade businesses, medical practices
  • Free initial consultation, custom pricing
  • Active content marketing (blog posts about AI consulting trends)
  • Why this matters: They explicitly target trade businesses. Overlaps with AOM's construction vertical. Florida-based, so not Phoenix competition, but same client type.
  • URL: https://authorityai.ai

Applied AI Advisor / 3A4AI (3a4ai.com) -- St. Petersburg / Tampa Bay, FL

  • "Your Fractional AI Officer"
  • Audits operations, designs AI infrastructure, trains teams
  • 30-minute free consultation
  • Target: small business owners, founders, solopreneurs
  • Pricing: not public
  • Why this matters: Solo operator model very similar to what AOM would run. Tampa Bay = similar market (Sun Belt small businesses). Worth studying their positioning.
  • URL: https://3a4ai.com

Estes Media (estesmedia.com)

  • AI consulting specifically for contractors, builders, architects
  • Free 30-min "AI Readiness & Opportunity Assessment" call
  • Help evaluate AI tools for lead gen, email outreach, chatbots, voice assistants
  • Also does digital marketing (dual service model like AOM)
  • Why this matters: HIGHEST THREAT. Already selling AI consulting to contractors. Same vertical as AOM. Same dual-service model. Watch closely.
  • URL: https://estesmedia.com

AI SMB Solutions (aismbsolutions.com)

  • AI Opportunity Blueprint, org chart overlay, tool matrix
  • Creates 3-10 custom GPTs per client, prompt packages
  • Audits by role and department
  • Why this matters: Template-driven approach. Not building real systems, more like "here's some GPTs for your team." AOM's multi-agent approach is fundamentally different and more valuable.
  • URL: https://www.aismbsolutions.com

Tier B: Fractional AI Officer Services

The FS Agency (fsagency.co) -- Denver, CO

  • Fractional Chief AI Officer services
  • Pricing: $5,000-$15,000/month
  • Focus: professional services (law firms, accounting firms, marketing agencies)
  • Weekly/biweekly strategy sessions with leadership
  • Phone: 303-578-8299
  • Why this matters: They specifically target professional services with fractional AI leadership. Their pricing is higher than AOM's planned range, which means AOM could undercut while offering more (creative + AI).
  • URL: https://fsagency.co

PrimeAI Solutions (primeai.solutions)

  • Fractional AI Officers, 2 days/month to 3 days/week
  • Free initial consultation
  • Focus: digital transformation + strategic consulting
  • Why this matters: Flexible engagement model worth studying.
  • URL: https://www.primeai.solutions

GAI Insights (gaiinsights.com)

  • Fractional CAIO services
  • Industry standard: $2,000-$8,000/month for 8-20 hours
  • URL: https://gaiinsights.com

AI First Mindset (aifirstmindset.ai)

  • Fractional CAIO
  • URL: https://aifirstmindset.ai

Head of AI (headofai.ai)

  • Marketplace of fractional CAIOs for hire
  • Pricing: $2,500-$30,000/month depending on scope
  • URL: https://headofai.ai

Momentum AI (momentumhub.ai)

  • Fractional CAIO starting at $2,500/month
  • URL: https://www.momentumhub.ai

Tier C: White-Label / Platform Plays

These aren't direct competitors but define what "surface-level" AI agencies are building with:

Stammer AI (stammer.ai)

  • White-label AI agent platform for agencies
  • 1,300+ agencies using it
  • Agencies charge clients $300-$500/month per agent
  • Setup fees on top
  • Usage: $0.001-$0.03 per message
  • Full white-label (your brand, your logo)
  • Why this matters: This is what most "AI agencies" actually are. They reskin Stammer, sell chatbots for $300-$500/month, and call it AI consulting. AOM builds real systems. Night and day difference.
  • URL: https://stammer.ai

Trillet (trillet.ai)

  • White-label chatbot platform
  • Studio: $99/month (3 sub-accounts), Agency: $299/month (unlimited)
  • 5-minute agent creation from website scraping
  • URL: https://www.trillet.ai

BizSage (bizsage.io)

  • White-label AI chatbot platform
  • Auto-crawls client websites to build agents
  • URL: https://bizsage.io

Lety.ai (lety.ai)

  • White-label AI "employees" for agencies to resell
  • URL: https://www.lety.ai

Tier D: Claude Code Consulting (Emerging)

KIBO Studios (kibostudios.com) -- Marbella/Madrid, Spain

  • Specialized Claude Code consulting
  • Enterprise implementation, custom MCP development, CI/CD integration
  • Rates: $30-70/hour (general), Claude-specific likely higher
  • Free first consultation
  • Why this matters: One of the few agencies specifically offering Claude Code implementation. AOM is already running Claude Code in production. KIBO is selling what AOM lives.
  • URL: https://www.kibostudios.com/en/claude-code

Kaizen AI Consulting (kaizenaiconsulting.com) -- UK

  • Claude Code implementation + strategy for UK businesses
  • Specific content on: construction firms using Claude for tender analysis, building internal tools, quote calculators
  • Claims clients save 10-15 hours/week
  • Why this matters: They literally have a case study on construction firms using Claude. Direct overlap with AOM's vision. But UK-based. And they don't have a running multi-agent system -- they consult on Claude usage, not agent architectures.
  • URL: https://kaizenaiconsulting.com

ALM Corp (almcorp.com)

  • Claude Cowork plugins, enterprise deployment
  • White-label Claude deployment for agencies
  • URL: https://almcorp.com

Tier E: Phoenix / Arizona Specifically

Opinosis Analytics (opinosis-analytics.com) -- Dr. Kavita Ganesan

  • AI consulting in Phoenix
  • Focus: custom ML models for businesses
  • Clients include 3M, Microsoft, eBay (enterprise-leaning)
  • URL: https://www.opinosis-analytics.com/ai-consulting-in-phoenix/

Ademero (ademero.com) -- Phoenix

  • AI consulting starting at $5,000/month for small businesses
  • Custom enterprise packages
  • URL: https://www.ademero.com

God Digital Marketing -- Phoenix

  • AI consulting specialists with 5+ years experience
  • Workflow optimization focus
  • URL: https://www.goddigitalmarketing.com

Nobody in Phoenix is doing creative production + AI ops for construction. The lane is wide open locally.

2. What Are They Offering

Common Product Types (ranked by frequency)

  1. AI Chatbots / Customer Support Bots -- The most common "AI service." White-label platforms make this trivially easy. Price: $300-$500/month ongoing, $2,000-$15,000 setup.

  2. AI Readiness Audits -- Discovery + roadmap. 2-4 weeks. Price: $2,000-$15,000. Every serious agency offers this as the entry point.

  3. Workflow Automation -- Connecting tools with Make/n8n/Zapier + AI layer on top. Price: $5,000-$50,000 per build.

  4. Custom GPTs / Knowledge Bases -- Private ChatGPT trained on company data. Price: $3,000-$10,000 setup + $200-$1,000/month.

  5. Voice Agents -- AI phone answering, appointment booking. Growing fast. Tech: Vapi, Retell AI, ElevenLabs. Price: $5,000-$25,000 setup + usage.

  6. Fractional AI Leadership -- Ongoing strategic advisory. Price: $2,000-$15,000/month.

  7. AI Training / Workshops -- Teaching teams to use AI tools. Price: $2,000-$5,000 per session.

Tech Stacks in Use

Competitor Primary Stack
LeftClick (Saraev) n8n, Make.com, GPT-4, custom Python
Morningside AI Custom builds, enterprise integrations
HummingAgent Custom AI, GPT, SOC 2 infra

Kaizen AI Claude Code, Claude API
KIBO Studios Claude Code, MCP servers

Estes Media Off-shelf AI tools + marketing stack

Are they building real agent systems?

Almost nobody is building multi-agent systems for clients.

  • The vast majority of "AI agencies" are reselling white-label chatbots (Stammer, Voiceflow, Botpress)
  • A smaller group builds legitimate workflow automations (n8n, Make) with AI nodes
  • An even smaller group builds custom AI applications (LeftClick, HummingAgent, Morningside)
  • NOBODY we found is building multi-agent orchestration systems (Mom > Bobby > Elmo pipeline) for SMB clients

This is AOM's widest moat. Everyone else is selling point solutions. AOM can sell a system.

Revenue Models

Model Who Uses It
One-time project fee Most agencies (audit + build)
Monthly retainer Fractional CAIOs, managed service agencies
SaaS markup White-label chatbot resellers
Course/community Liam Ottley, Nick Saraev, Corbin Brown
Hybrid (project + retainer) LeftClick, FS Agency, AOM's planned model

The agencies making the most money combine project fees with ongoing retainers. One-off projects don't scale. The retainer is the play -- same as AOM's social media model.

3. What They're Doing Well

Best Landing Pages / Positioning

HummingAgent -- Clean, benefit-driven copy. "Save 66% on operations." Shows the math. Local pages for every city (SEO play). Good trust signals.

LeftClick AI -- Minimal. Lets Nick's personal brand do the selling. The website is almost a formality. All lead gen comes from YouTube + Skool.

Authority AI -- Strong blog content marketing. Multiple articles ranking for "AI business consulting" terms. Good industry-specific pages (law, insurance, trades).

Stammer AI -- Best white-label platform marketing. Clear agency economics spelled out (charge clients $300-$500/month, your cost is pennies). Makes it feel like printing money.

Best Positioning / Messaging

Nick Saraev / LeftClick: "I built a one-person business doing $72K/month with AI. Here's how." Personal proof > corporate claims. His content IS the marketing.

Liam Ottley / Morningside: Coined the entire category. "AI Automation Agency" is his term. That's unbeatable positioning -- he defined the space.

FS Agency: "Your law firm doesn't need a full-time AI executive. You need a fractional one." Clean, specific, obvious next step.

Estes Media: "AI consulting specifically for contractors." Verticalized messaging that speaks directly to the audience.

Best Case Studies / Proof Points

  • HummingAgent: claims 66% operational savings across clients
  • MQLFlow: claims 1,200% average ROI
  • Kaizen AI: "Construction firm uses Claude for tender document analysis" -- directly relevant to AOM's target
  • Nick Saraev: $72K/month personal income is the case study itself
  • Liam Ottley: $7M+ revenue at Morningside, 40+ employees
  • House of Growth (content agency): doubled output from 80 to 160 articles/month, saved 85+ hours/month with AI

Who Has the Most Traction

  1. Liam Ottley -- 700K YouTube, 280K Skool, $7M+ revenue. Category creator.
  2. Nick Saraev -- 220K YouTube, 400K Instagram, $72K/month service business
  3. Stammer AI -- 1,300+ agencies using the platform
  4. Allie K. Miller -- 2M LinkedIn followers, #1 AI Business voice on LinkedIn
  5. Jordan Wilson / Everyday AI -- Top 10 tech podcast on Spotify
  6. Sabrina Ramonov -- Massive YouTube/TikTok/Substack following for AI automation tutorials

4. What They're Doing Poorly

Gap 1: Chatbot Theater

The VAST majority of "AI agencies" are reselling white-label chatbots and calling it "AI transformation." A Stammer chatbot that answers FAQ is not an AI system. It's a slightly smarter Zendesk widget. Clients are starting to figure this out. The 2026 market is already seeing pushback: "I paid $5K for a chatbot and it doesn't do anything my website form didn't do."

AOM's advantage: Real systems that automate real workflows, not just chat interfaces.

Gap 2: No Creative Production

Every AI consulting agency we found is purely technical. They build bots and automations. NONE of them also produce video, design brands, build websites, or manage social media. They can't show a client "here's your new website AND here's the AI system that powers your operations." AOM can.

AOM's advantage: One vendor for creative + AI. This is genuinely unique.

Gap 3: No Proof of Internal Use

Most AI agencies sell AI but don't visibly run on it. Their own operations are manual. Liam Ottley and Nick Saraev are exceptions (they talk about their own systems), but even they don't show a multi-agent pipeline.

AOM's advantage: The EA repo IS the proof. Bobby builds sites. Elmo QAs them. Mom orchestrates. Jacob does outreach. Cleo produces content. This is a running, documented, production system. Nobody else has this.

Gap 4: Construction Vertical is Unowned

Estes Media is the only agency explicitly targeting contractors with AI consulting, and even they are more marketing-focused than operations-focused. Nobody is doing AI operational systems (scheduling, estimating, crew management, project tracking) for construction companies.

AOM's advantage: Already in the vertical. Already has construction clients. Already understands the pain points.

Gap 5: No Multi-Agent Architecture

Nobody is selling multi-agent orchestration to SMBs. The enterprise world has CrewAI, AutoGen, and LangGraph frameworks, but nobody is packaging that into an SMB product. Everyone is selling single-purpose bots.

AOM's advantage: AOM's pipeline (Elon > Mom > Alex > Steffen > Bobby > Elmo > Patrik) is exactly the kind of system that could be productized. Imagine a construction company with: a scheduling agent, an estimating agent, a customer communication agent, and a QA agent that checks everything before it goes to the client. That's AOM's product.

Gap 6: Course Sellers vs. Service Providers

A huge chunk of this market is people selling courses ABOUT starting AI agencies rather than actually running agencies that serve clients. Liam's AAA Accelerator, Corbin Brown's course, dozens of Udemy/Skool programs. The course sellers outnumber the actual practitioners maybe 10:1.

AOM's advantage: AOM does the work. Not teaching about doing the work.

Gap 7: No Ongoing Relationship

Most competitors sell a project and walk away. Audit, build, done. The fractional CAIO model has retention, but it's expensive ($5K-$15K/month). There's a gap between "one-time $5K build" and "$5K/month fractional executive." AOM's $1,500-$3,000/month retainer model fills that gap.

Potential Partners vs. Competitors

Partner opportunities:

  • Allie K. Miller -- Her audience is business leaders who need AI. AOM builds the AI. Potential referral relationship.
  • Jordan Wilson / Everyday AI -- Could feature AOM as a case study. "How a creative agency runs on AI agents."
  • Greg Isenberg -- Always looking for interesting AI business stories. AOM's multi-agent system is exactly the kind of thing he'd feature.
  • Sabrina Ramonov -- Her audience is DIY builders. AOM serves the people who tried DIY and failed.

Direct competition:

  • Nick Saraev / LeftClick -- Same service model, different vertical
  • Liam Ottley's students -- Thousands of them. Most will fail, but some will be real competitors
  • Authority AI -- Same vertical overlap (trades)
  • Estes Media -- Highest direct threat (contractors + AI consulting)

6. AOM's Competitive Position (Summary)

What AOM Has That Nobody Else Does

  1. A running multi-agent production system. Not a demo. Not a concept. A daily-use system with Bobby (web), Elmo (QA), Mom (orchestration), Jacob (outreach), Cleo (content), Alex (strategy), Steffen (brand), Tony (social). This is proof, not theory.

  2. Creative + AI in one vendor. Video production, web development, brand design, social media, AND AI operations. Every competitor is one or the other. AOM is both.

  3. Construction vertical depth. Already serving construction clients. Already understands the pain points. Already has relationships.

  4. Retainer DNA. AOM already runs $2-3.5K/month retainers for social media. Adding AI ops is an upsell, not a cold sell. The trust is already built.

  5. Phoenix market. Nobody in Phoenix is doing this for construction companies. Local presence matters for this vertical. These are people who want to shake your hand.

Where AOM Needs to Catch Up

  1. Content / thought leadership. Nick Saraev, Liam Ottley, and Allie K. Miller built audiences that generate leads on autopilot. AOM has zero content presence in the AI consulting space. Patrik's LinkedIn is the fastest path to fixing this.

  2. Case study documentation. Every successful competitor has documented ROI. "We saved client X hours/week." AOM needs to document its own internal case study (hours saved, tasks automated, agent output quality) and then its first client case study.

  3. Productized offering. The audit framework, the pricing tiers, the proposal template. These need to exist before the first sale. Steve and Alex already outlined this -- it needs to be built.

  4. Website presence. AI advisory services need to be on aheadofmarket.com. Even a single page with clear positioning would put AOM ahead of the agencies with no web presence.

Competitive Moat Ranking

Moat Strength Defensibility
Multi-agent system as proof Very Strong High (hard to replicate)
Creative + AI hybrid Strong Medium (someone could copy eventually)
Construction vertical Medium Low (others will enter)
Phoenix local presence Medium Medium (geography is a moat for in-person work)
Retainer relationships Strong High (switching costs are real)

7. Key Takeaways for AOM

  1. The market is real and growing fast. AI consulting for SMBs is a $11B+ market growing at 26-37% CAGR. This isn't speculative.

  2. Most competitors are shallow. White-label chatbot resellers calling themselves "AI agencies." AOM's depth is a genuine differentiator.

  3. Nobody owns construction + AI. Estes Media is closest but they're marketing-focused, not operations-focused. AOM can own this.

  4. Content is the lead gen engine. Every successful player in this space built an audience first. Patrik posting about running AOM on AI agents is the fastest path to credibility and leads.

  5. The multi-agent angle is uncharted for SMBs. Enterprise has CrewAI and frameworks. SMBs have nothing. AOM could be the first to productize this.

  6. Pricing is validated. $2,500 audit, $5-8K build, $1,500-$3K/month retainer is right in the market sweet spot. Not too cheap (looks amateur), not too expensive (scares off SMBs).

  7. Move now. The window is narrowing. In 2023, this was wide open. In 2026, competition is heating up. But construction + AI ops + creative production is still untouched. First mover advantage matters for local, relationship-driven verticals.
